descriptor.scene: NOBODY IS IN THIS PICTURE: no people, no figures anywhere, above ground or below. This is ONE continuous cutaway landscape in a single unbroken frame, never panels: one shared ground plane runs straight across the middle of the image, carrying two young skylines, and the earth below it is cut open to show what each city buried. Under the LEFT skyline, a clean subway line: one elegant tunnel drawn straight and true, evenly spaced arches, tidy track, and clearly ROOM left beside it for more lines to be added, with a gracefully capped stub where the next extension will join. Under the RIGHT skyline, a tangled one: tunnels crossing and doubling back, patched with mismatched braces, pipes rerouted around pipes, dead-end spurs, no room to add anything. The contrast reads left to right as order and margin against knot and patch. Above ground both cities are similar young pale towers in warm daylight; the difference is ALL underground. The sky along the top of the frame stays calm and open.
negatives: panel borders, split panels, a dividing line or a comic grid (one continuous cutaway image)
people, trains with visible passengers, or figures anywhere
lettering, route numbers or station signs
descriptor._caption: There are two ways to lay a subway under a young city. Tokyo laid lines it could extend, and extends them still. New York laid lines it can barely repair. What you bury badly, you live over forever. Maya lays the kind you can extend.

The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. If a person in this scene is moving toward something, that destination MUST BE AHEAD OF THEM IN THE FRAME and they must be seen FROM BEHIND or from three-quarters behind, so the viewer is following them into it. A figure whose face is toward the camera is walking AWAY from everything behind them: if the thing they are moving toward is drawn behind them, the picture says the opposite of the scene. Their feet, hips, shoulders and gaze all point the same way, along the direction of travel.
